summary: Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Hanazono University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), abbot at Shofuku-ji (~1949–1978), and head of The Institute for Zen Studies (1964).

Mun-keat Choong works in Buddhist studies. He studied at the Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute, Komazawa University, and the University of Queensland, completing his MA and PhD under Roderick S. Bucknell between 1992 and 1998.

Munenobu Sakurai is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral course at Tohoku University (~1986–1991). He served as an associate professor at Iwate University (~1996–2005) and became a professor at Tohoku University around 2005.

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indology and computational scholar who studied at Kyoto University and Harvard University (PhD ~1974–1981). He served as associate professor at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1981–1989) and as associate professor and professor at Kyoto University (~1989–2009).
Muneyoshi Yanagi (1889–1961) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki (~1906–1910) and at the University of Tokyo (~1910–1913).
Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under the doctoral supervision of Brigitte Marschall (attested 2010).

Munis D. Faruqui is a historian and Indologist. He has served as a professor and undergraduate advisor at the University of California, Berkeley (from ~2003) and as director and professor at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Murray B. Emeneau (1904–2005) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale under Franklin Edgerton, Edgar Howard Sturtevant, and Edward Sapir. He taught Latin at Yale (1926) and served as professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at UC Berkeley (1940–1971).

Musashi Tachikawa is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Nagoya University and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held posts at Nagoya University (1970), the National Museum of Ethnology (~1992–2007), and Aichi Gakuin University (~2007–2017).

Muzaffar Alam is a historian and Indologist who studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He taught at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1973–2001) and became George V. Bobrinskoy Professor at the University of Chicago around 2001.

Myles Dillon (1900–1972) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at University College Dublin and under Osborn Bergin, Rudolf Thurneysen, and Heinrich Zimmer. He held posts at Trinity College Dublin, University College Dublin, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies.
Myokyo-ni (1921–2007) worked in Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Graz, under Walter Nowick, and under traditional teacher Soko Morinaga in 1984.

Mysore Hiriyanna (1871–1950) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at Madras Christian College. He served as a librarian at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (1891) and as Assistant Professor and Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and the University of Mysore (~1912–1927).

Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas (1916–1999) worked in Indology, studying at Mysore, Mumbai, and Oxford. He taught at Oxford (~1948–1951), MS University of Baroda (~1951–1959), and the University of Delhi (1959), later serving as chairman of the Institute for Social and Economic Change (1972–1979).

Mónika Kiss is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She pursued doctoral studies in Japanese Studies at Eötvös Loránd University under the advisorship of Masanori Yamaji (attested 2016) and studied under Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.

N. A. Jayawickrama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He served as a professor at the University of Ceylon (~1958–1976) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1976–1985).
N. Aiyaswami Sastri was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).
N. D. Mironov (1880–1936) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1902–1903) and under Hermann Jacobi (~1903–1905) and Heinrich Hübschmann.

N. J. Francis is a scholar in Indology and ancient history who earned a master's in ancient history at the University of Calicut under the doctoral supervision of M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).

N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya (1928–2017) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Vice Chancellor of the National Sanskrit University (1989–1994) and worked as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1989–2017).
